The failure path pays the sweep again: `NoSymbol_Gradient_1144x168` 249 → 275 µs (+10 %), `NoSymbol_Noise_1144x168` 6.45 → 6.43 ms (0/255 noise, so no regional pass).

**A review round on the test** found two of the six renders sound only by accident: Micro QR turned exactly 180° at a half-pixel x offset puts most crisp pixel centres exactly on a module edge, so which module each shows follows the sign of `MathF.Sin(π)`'s residue and some modules come out 1 or 3 px wide; at 0.49 or 0.51 they read without the sweep. They were replaced by crisp renders with no pixel centre on an edge that still need the sweep (37° at (0.5, 1.5) under the shadow, 53° at (0.5, 2.5) under a downward ramp), all six red with the sweep skipped. The renderer's unused fractional-scale form was removed and its turned form's summary says what its offset is (pixels, whole or fractional, from a point 1.5 px above the centre). Lesson: a render parameter at an exact tie (half-pixel offset at a right-angle turn) tests the rounding, not the geometry; a case that needs a fallback has to keep needing it when nudged.

**A second review round on the test** found the replacements still narrow: rMQR 20° at (0.5, 1.5) read only within 0.05° of its turn and a few hundredths of a pixel of its offset even with the sweep, and four of the other five had nudges that read without the sweep or not at all. A search over 12,960 renders (2 px/module, both symbologies, crisp and anti-aliased, turns 1-89°, three x and eight y offsets, three lights) scored each render that needs the sweep against 20 nudges (turn ±0.1/0.2/0.5°, each offset ±0.02/0.05/0.1 px, depth ±0.03); the six now in the test read with the sweep and fail without it at all 20, and all six are red with the sweep skipped. The renderer's class summary no longer calls every render crisp at a whole scale, the turned form states the offsets that keep its two-module margin, and the shared spec-map row names the full sweep for Micro QR and rMQR only (Standard QR's attempt widens inside `TryFind`). Lesson: a regression case has two conditions, and the one forgotten is that the path under test must still read around the chosen point; a case that fails when nudged fails for the next unrelated change.

**A third review round on the test** found the 20-nudge search too coarse: sampled densely (turn every 0.025° to ±0.5°, each offset every 0.005 px to ±0.1 px, depth every 0.005 to ±0.03), three of the six read without the sweep between the sampled nudges, and two failed even with it where two nudges combine (turn and depth). The candidates were checked again at those 136 axis steps and the 81 corners of the nudge box; twenty pass both everywhere, none of them under the shadow or anti-aliased rMQR, and the test now holds five of them plus rMQR anti-aliased 33° at (0, 2.5) under a downward ramp, which passes every axis step and reads without the sweep at 3 of the 81 corners. All six are red with the sweep skipped. The first review's reason for the earlier no-loss results was also wrong and is corrected above and in the spec: the turned and offset sets were evenly lit, so their finders between scanned rows were read by the global attempts. A probe from the same review found a second way to need the sweep: eight or more finder-like marks outrank the real finder in the strided scan's candidate list, which tries eight, and 1,254 of 12,288 renders with ten decoys read only with the sweep. Lesson: a robustness claim is only as fine as its sampling; state the grid it was checked on, or check it densely.

**A fourth review round on the test** confirmed the cause per case: on each render's regional binarization the strided `FindCandidates` returns no candidate, and the full sweep returns one, the real finder, so no decoy crowds it out. The test comment now claims robustness per axis only (the anti-aliased rMQR case reads without the sweep at 15 of 625 points of a 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 nudge grid), the renderer's class summary says which form needs the quiet zone in the grid, and the cost-round entry points here.

**A fifth review round on the test** found the test trusted its premise: it asserted a decode only, so a later change that let the strided scan read these renders would leave it green and guarding nothing. Each case now first asserts, on its regional binarization, that the strided `FindCandidates` finds no finder and the full sweep does (an axis-aligned control fails there), and asserts `Success` like the other uneven-light tests. The comment states the nudge range, the summary no longer reads as if the global attempts read these renders, and the spec's 880 is per set.

**A sixth review round on the test** found the other half of the premise unchecked: nothing asserted that the global attempts fail on these renders, and if one read them the regional attempt would never run. Each case now also asserts that neither global polarity decodes (`DecodeLuminanceCore` of each decoder, strided scan and sweep, is internal for it; an evenly lit control fails there).

### Phase 3, branch review: limits stated, premises exact (2026-09-23)

**Done.** An adversarial review of the whole branch against `main` (the binarizer against an independent port of ZXing's `HybridBinarizer` on 20,000 random cases in three SIMD configurations: no mismatch) left eight findings after three votes each:
- **A soft shadow is read only while it takes less than half the light when the modules line up with the 8 × 8 blocks.** At 8 and 16 px/module, whole pixels, every block is flat and takes the lit side's black point (paper 220 → 110), so a shadow taking half or more reads its paper as ink and only 4 to 6 of 8 directions decode (ZXing.Net's hybrid binarizer the same without its rotation retries; zxing-cpp reads none at 8 px). The public remarks, README and spec were narrowed to a shadow under half the light (and in the second round below to 40 %). Reading past half on aligned grids is a candidate for later work, not a defect of this port.
- **16 of the 96 lit decode cases never needed the regional pass**: the global threshold reads Standard QR ramp 45°, Micro QR ramps 45/135/315° and rMQR ramps 0/45/135/315°, and their premise (a tenth of the paper read as ink) did not notice. Each lit case now asserts which pass reads it, both ways, through the decoders' internal `DecodeLuminanceCore` (Standard QR's made internal too); a later change that lets the global threshold read more turns the list red instead of silently.
- **The flat rule's two boundaries were untested**: `range <= 24` → `< 24` and `min < neighbours` → `<=` both passed the whole suite. The parity test gains levels 24 and 25 apart and a flat block at its neighbours' level (867 cases); each mutation now fails 72.
- **`charsWritten` leaked from the attempt that got furthest**: a mirrored negative under uneven light reaches its bitstream only in the last regional attempt, and a bitstream that fails after writing text returned false with five characters written. `main` had the same leak through the inverted retry. Every decoder now reports 0 on total failure (`StandardQR_UnevenLightBitstreamFailsPartWay_WritesNoCharacters`).
- **Images under 33 px a side get no regional pass** (no 5 × 5 neighbourhood of blocks; ZXing stops at 40), now stated in the public remarks and the spec.
- Four texts: the spec's "no reader past 65 %" (every reader reads 2 of 8 at 75 %, none at 85 %), the sweep's +400 mixing Micro QR into Standard QR's total, "well-lit" left in `FinderPatternFinder`, and the flat rule described as "top and left" where it is the 1:2:1 mean of top, left and top-left.

Not kept: the skip being unproven when grey levels give the finder a second look (no reproduction).

**Lessons.** A premise that is necessary is not sufficient: "the global threshold reads part of the paper as ink" was true of cases the global threshold still read. State which path reads a case and assert it both ways. And a reference written from the same description as the code shares its boundaries: a parity test only guards a boundary its inputs sit on.

**A second round** found the first round's own promise false and three more gaps, each kept after three votes:
- **"Under half the light" failed below half.** Swept 0.20-0.65 over Standard QR versions 1-5 at every level, Micro QR M1-M4 and rMQR R7x43, R11x27 and R13x43, 2-16 px/module, eight directions: every direction reads up to 42 %, and the first failures are at 43 % (Standard QR version 1-H on 8 px modules) and 44 % (2 px). The test at 0.45 passed only because its version 3-M symbol is among the strongest, and the global threshold read all 48 of its cases, so it guarded nothing of the regional pass. The public docs now promise a soft-edged shadow of up to 40 %; `UnevenLight_ShadowUpToFortyPercent_Decodes` (168: three symbologies, seven scales, eight directions, Standard QR at version 1-H) holds it, and `UnevenLight_ShadowPastHalfOnBlockAlignedModules_RegionalPassDecodes` (4, at 55 % on 8 px modules) asserts the global attempts fail and the regional pass reads.
- **A content verdict was lost to "report the first attempt".** A symbol only the regional pass reaches, holding a Kanji cell with no JIS X 0208 mapping, reached the caller as `NotDetected`, not the `UnmappedCharacter` a caller branches on to fall back to a CP932 reader; twice over, since the retry also returned the negative's `NotDetected` over the positive's verdict. `main` had the same loss for a reversed symbol through the inverted retry. A verdict on the symbol's content (`UnmappedCharacter`, `UnsupportedContent`) now outranks an attempt that found nothing, in the retry and in each decoder's report (`RegionalRetryTest.Decode_ContentVerdict_OutranksANegativeThatFoundNothing`, `KanjiUnmappedCharacterEndToEndTest.UnmappedCell_ReadOnlyByALaterAttempt_ReachesTheCaller`).
- **The image path's `charsWritten` of 0 on failure was undocumented**, and differs from the matrix path, which reports the partial count; the three `TryDecodeImage` span overloads now say so. The Micro QR and rMQR resets never change a value their scans already zero; they stay as the place the contract is kept.
- Three texts: the black point "from its own range" (it is the mean), the Tier 1 row without the 33 px condition, and one three-module shadow edge called soft in the public docs and sharp in the spec (now soft-edged throughout, the measured edge named).

**Lessons.** A bound checked on the test's own symbol is a bound on that symbol: the worst case sat two versions away. And a test that promises to exercise a path has to assert that it does; the first round wrote that rule and then broke it in its own new test.

**A third round** found the second round's `charsWritten` contract false and its status rule half-built, each kept after three votes:
- **`DestinationTooSmall` returned a partial count.** A Standard QR of 40 digits then "abc" (Optimal segmentation) into a 40-character destination returned false with 40 written: the status is terminal, so the reset on total failure never ran. Each decoder's `DecodeLuminance` is now a wrapper that reports 0 on any status but `Success` (`StandardQR_DestinationShortOfTheSecondSegment_WritesNoCharacters`), which also retires the Micro QR and rMQR resets that never changed a value.
- **A first attempt's content verdict still ran every other attempt**, the regional pass included (two binarizations on any image with grey), then reported the first status anyway: roughly twice the time for every GS1 or unmapped-Kanji symbol. A verdict now ends the attempts wherever it is reached (first, inverted, regional); only another symbol in the image could have changed the answer.
- **The rule had no test outside Standard QR and one unguarded branch.** `ContentVerdictImageDecodeTest` builds Micro QR M4-L and rMQR R11x43-M symbols with a Kanji cell from real codewords and reads the unmapped cell as `UnmappedCharacter` through each path (first, inverted, regional), with a mappable control; `RegionalRetryTest` adds a negative `Success` and `DestinationTooSmall` after a positive verdict.
- **`InvalidBitstream` and `DataUncorrectable` stay out of the verdicts**, now said where the rule is: noise reaches the second in the regional pass (the no-symbol test turns red when it counts), and the first through a miscorrection, notably on Micro QR M1, whose codewords only detect errors. The rule is in the spec (`qrcode-symbologies.md`, next to `UnmappedCharacter`), and the texts that said a verdict outranks "an attempt that found nothing" say "a failure short of the content".
- The lighting paragraph said the global threshold stops past 45 % and the first failure is at 43 %: the first is the version 3 symbol tested, the second a small version. Both are now attributed, and the test's own symbol first fails at 44 %.

**A fourth round** found the third round's early exit a regression and the verdict rule broken inside the attempts it did not touch, each kept after three votes:
- **The first-attempt exit lost a read `main` made.** Beside an unmapped symbol, a light-on-dark readable one is read by the inverted retry; ending on the first attempt's verdict returned `UnmappedCharacter` where `main` returned the text, in all three symbologies. The first attempt and the inverted retry now run as on `main`; a verdict from either skips only the regional pass, which looks for a symbol the global threshold cannot see, and a verdict proves it was seen. That keeps the saving the third round was after (no binarization for a GS1 or unmapped-Kanji symbol) without changing any read. In the regional pass a positive verdict now ends it, so `RegionalRetry` lost its preference branch (`ContentVerdictImageDecodeTest.UnmappedSymbolBesideAReversedReadableOne_ReadsTheReadableOne`, `RegionalRetryTest.Decode_PositiveContentVerdict_StopsThere`).
- **Inside an attempt the verdict still lost, as on `main`.** Micro QR and rMQR rank failures across the grids they try for one symbol, and ranked a verdict equal to `DataUncorrectable`, keeping whichever came first: a Micro QR M4-L unmapped symbol turned 7° reported `DataUncorrectable` in 59 to 69 of 72-92 renders. Standard QR's mirror retry kept the unmirrored grid's `FormatInformationInvalid` over the mirrored grid's verdict. A verdict now ranks with `DestinationTooSmall`, and the mirror retry prefers it (`UnmappedCell_Turned_ReachesTheCallerAsUnmappedCharacter`, `StandardQR_UnmappedCellMirrored_ReachesTheCallerAsUnmappedCharacter`).
- **The searches inside Micro QR and rMQR attempts keep going after a verdict** (2-19 ms for an unmapped symbol, as on `main`): speed with no result to change, so it joins phase 3b's levers.
- Texts: the flat bound (a range of exactly 24 is flat), the 12 px shadow bound (59 %, not 56 %) and the sweep's payload ("12345"), and the rMQR pipeline diagram and chain, which ended at the inverted retry.

Seen on the way and left for its own work: a Micro QR symbol turned 30° holding Kanji 0x8794 decodes as `Success` with "95549", a false read of another grid, on `main` too.

**A fifth round** found the rule still broken inside attempts and one regression from the fourth, each kept after three votes; a sweep against `main` found no read lost (134,878 synthetic renders and the 624 corpus images: 0 lost, 84 corpus reads gained, `qrcode-5` misreads 16 → 0) and no verdict from noise:
- **Fallbacks inside an attempt still dropped a verdict**: Standard QR's timing frame, other dimensions, mesh and finder-only grid, and the full finder sweep of Micro QR and rMQR, each let a verdict lose to the failure of the grid chosen against it (the timing frame and the mesh run first, and a later grid's failure overwrote their verdict; the others ran after a failure and were not returned). 52 of 1,476 low-density renders (1-3 px/module, crisp and anti-aliased) reached `UnmappedCharacter` inside and reported `DataUncorrectable` or `NotDetected`. Each decoder now has `IsSettled` (read, too long, or a verdict) at those points (`UnmappedCell_ReadByAFallbackInsideTheAttempt_ReachesTheCallerAsUnmappedCharacter`, which also pins the rMQR ranking the fourth round left untested).
- **The fourth round's mirror-retry exit broke an invariant**: returning on an unmirrored verdict before transposing left the finder-only fallback comparing its sampling against the wrong orientation, one redundant decode per verdict on version 2+. A verdict now returns before that fallback, so the comparison only ever sees a transposed first grid.
- The wrapper's comment named a short destination and a verdict; the case its test guards is a later attempt that failed part-way through its bitstream.

Seen on the way, on `main` too, and left with the other false read for its own work: a Micro QR M4-L unmapped symbol, anti-aliased at 1.60 px/module, offset 0.66, reads as version M1 "0824" (M1 only detects errors).

**A sixth round** found the fifth's own change too wide, each kept after three votes:
- **A strided verdict skipped the full sweep and lost a readable neighbour.** Two symbols side by side, an unmapped one the strided scan finds and a mappable one at 1.0-2.5 px/module only the sweep finds: Micro QR read 422-430 of 488-496 pairs against `main`'s 442-450, rMQR 424-432 against 448-454, every loss `main`'s `Success` turned `UnmappedCharacter`. The strided scan returns early on a terminal status again; the sweep's verdict is still reported (`UnmappedSymbolBesideALowDensityReadableOne_ReadsTheReadableOne`).
- **Four Standard QR sites had no test that could reach them**: the timing-counted, version-named and runner-up dimensions and the finder-only grid, reverted one at a time, changed 2-60 unmapped renders each and failed nothing, because the only Kanji builder made version 1. It now builds any version (blocks interleaved, version information placed from 7), and `StandardQR_UnmappedCellReadByALaterGrid_ReachesTheCallerAsUnmappedCharacter` holds one render per site (versions 5, 3, 2 and 8).
- Texts: the spec called the timing frame and the mesh fallbacks after a failure (both run first), said a verdict "settles the search the way a read does" (the Micro QR and rMQR scans still run their candidates), and three comments still said `DestinationTooSmall` outranks every failure, which a verdict now shares.

**Lesson.** A rule stated for "the symbol" has to be checked against the image: stopping a search because one symbol gave a verdict also stops it for every other symbol in the image, and the envelope contract (never narrower than a full sweep's) is about the image.

**A seventh round** found no defect in the decode logic and four gaps, each kept after three votes; a probe of 8,090 images (all three decoders, single and two-symbol, noise) lost no read against `main`:
- **The mesh's verdict had no test**: reverting it failed nothing, yet a version 35-L unmapped symbol keystoned 11 % is read only by the mesh (`StandardQR_UnmappedCellReadByTheMesh_ReachesTheCallerAsUnmappedCharacter`, which the Kanji builder reaches now that it builds any version).
- **The regional pass gave Micro QR false reads `main` did not**: inverted, turned, shadowed rMQR images read by the Micro QR decoder as M1 symbols (M1 only detects errors), 12 of 6,400 against `main`'s 3, the 9 extra all through the regional pass. The Micro QR regional attempt now refuses an M1 result (`MicroQR_UnevenLightRmQRImage_NoFalseRead`); the user chose that over keeping the reads. It costs 36 Micro QR sweep reads the pass had added (bilinear upscales of M1 at 2-2.5 px/module), so the Micro QR sweep gain against `main` is +9, not +45; the corpus is unchanged (60 → 64). Recovering those reads with a structural M1 check belongs with the Micro QR false reads `main` already has, set aside for their own work.
- **Corrections to earlier entries**: the fifth round's "84 corpus reads gained, `qrcode-5` misreads 16 → 0" compared against a `main` run whose expected texts had CRLF where the decoded ones have LF; against the canonical baseline the corpus gains 68 (Standard QR 64, Micro QR 4) with no misread on either side. The fourth round's "speed with no result to change" for the searches after a verdict was disproved by the sixth, and the 3b row no longer lists that stop as a lever.
- Texts: `LocalBinarizer` joins the SIMD tier inventory, the Micro QR and rMQR envelope statements carry the lighting support the public docs promise, the spec says that a verdict skipping the regional pass also skips a second, unevenly lit symbol beside it, and the Kanji test's summary no longer says every failure retries.

**An eighth round** found the M1 refusal incomplete and its documentation too broad, each kept after three votes; a random mix of 21,000 images and a focused 90,000 lost no read against `main` and gave no new Standard QR or rMQR misread:
- **An empty M2 read still got through**: an inverted, turned, shadowed rMQR image read by the Micro QR decoder as M2 with no text, 2 errors corrected toward an all-zero data word (numeric, count 0), about 1 in 30,000 focused renders, `main` reading nothing. The Micro QR regional attempt now also refuses a successful read with no text (`MicroQR_UnevenLightRmQRImage_NoEmptyRead`); `DestinationTooSmall` stays, since a short destination reports no text either.
- **The 40 % promise is not M1's**: the global threshold alone loses a turned or anti-aliased M1 symbol from about 30 % (a 2.2 px/module render turned 322° from 29 %), on `main` too, where the regional pass had carried it to 40 %. The public docs and the spec now scope lighting to M2 and larger, and the spec's ramp sentence to the symbols that read at 80 % (rMQR R7x43 loses 2 of 8 directions).
- **Two tests pin the refusal's edges**: an M1 symbol under a shadow is not read by the regional pass even into a short destination (`MicroQR_M1UnevenLight_NotReadByTheRegionalPass`), and an M2 symbol is (`MicroQR_M2UnevenLight_ReadByTheRegionalPass`); before, narrowing the refusal to `Success` or widening it to M2 passed the suite. The refusal's state resets were dead (the negative polarity or the caller overwrote them) and are gone.
- Texts: the Kanji test's summary (the inverted retry runs on any failure), a plan identifier on an rMQR spec line this branch rewrote.

**A ninth round** kept four findings after three votes each and dropped one (a content verdict still costs Micro QR about 10 ms and rMQR about 2 ms, the same on `main`: the candidate scans this branch did not change search every refinement of a finder whose grid gave a verdict):
- **The 40 % promise held only on crisp renders**: the shadow was measured with the whole-scale renderer, crisp and axis-aligned. Anti-aliased edges hold 40 % from 3.5 px/module, turned or not (0 of 7,040 directions lost from 3.5 to 6 px/module over Standard QR versions 1-5, Micro QR M2 and M3 and three rMQR versions, turns to 45°); at 3 px/module a symbol turned 45° loses a direction or two from 30 %, at 2.5 px/module 222 of 1,760 directions are lost at 40 %, and at 2 px/module losses start at 20 %. The public docs and specs now carry "from 3.5 px a module when edges are anti-aliased", and `UnevenLight_AntiAliasedShadowUpToFortyPercent_Decodes` pins it (three symbologies, three turns, eight directions at 3.5 px/module).
- **A refused M1 read ended the Micro QR regional attempt**: the refusal judged the attempt's result, so an M1 grid read first stopped the candidate loop and skipped the sweep, and an M3 beside it that only the regional pass reads was lost (46 of 144 pair images at 45-65 %, `main` reading neither). The refusal now judges each grid inside the scan, which goes on to the next grid or candidate, and all 46 read the M3 (`MicroQR_M1BesideM3UnevenLight_RegionalPassReadsTheM3`); the Micro QR sweep against `main` is unchanged (+9, none lost, no misread).
- **A verdict skipping the regional pass had no test**: removing the first attempt's check passed the suite in all three decoders, and it is observable (beside an evenly lit unmapped symbol, a shadowed readable one is then read). `UnmappedSymbolBesideAShadowedReadableOne_ReportsTheVerdict` pins the documented behaviour.
- **The Micro QR `charsWritten` reset had no test**: a reflectance-reversed M1 under a shadow reached the caller as `NotDetected` with 5 characters counted once the reset was removed. With the refusal inside the scan every failure already counts 0, so the reset is now a guard; `MicroQR_M1UnevenLight_NotReadByTheRegionalPass` covers both polarities with the span overload. The refused text can stay in the destination, so the public docs now say the destination may hold text "from an attempt that was not kept".

**A tenth round** kept seven findings after three votes each:
- **The 40 % promise needed a density floor and a margin**: a crisp symbol under 2 px/module can lose every direction at 40 % (1 to 1.75 px/module, where the spec says crisp renders read), and a margin wider than the quiet zone makes the global threshold split lit paper from shadowed paper, which the regional pass does not make up for on block-aligned modules (8 px/module from 38 % with an 8-module margin, from 26 % with 20 to 30). Within the new wording, "from 2 px a module or 3.5 when edges are anti-aliased, with no more margin than the quiet zone", a sweep of Standard QR versions 1-5, Micro QR M2-M4 and three rMQR versions at both levels lost 0 of 8,016 crisp and 0 of 19,200 anti-aliased directions at 40 %. The spec's numbers were corrected with it: anti-aliased losses at 2 px/module start at 17-20 % axis-aligned and 10 % turned, not 20 %; crisp turned symbols at 2 px/module lose a direction at 40 % in more cases than the one named; the deeper-shadow limits are 56, 61 and 59 % on whole-scale renders and 55 and 57 % with sub-pixel offsets.
- **A refused M1 cost the whole search**: judging each grid let the arbitrary-orientation, scale and perspective searches go on sampling the same finder, about 2,000 to 17,000 grid decodes, so an M1 symbol under a shadow failed in 3-6 ms where `main` fails in 0.03 ms. A refused grid now ends its candidate's search, and the scan goes on to the next candidate: 0.09-0.66 ms, with the M1-beside-M3 read kept.
- **Real symbols with no text were refused**: the empty-read refusal took a Micro QR M3 or M4 symbol holding no text, a valid symbol, for texture (159 and 174 of 480 anti-aliased renders read only by the regional pass lost). The refusal now needs the read to have corrected errors, which the known false read did (2) and a real empty symbol read cleanly does not (`MicroQR_EmptySymbolUnevenLight_ReadByTheRegionalPass`).
- **The refusal on the low-density path had no test**: the module-boundary grids under 1.5 px/module passed 593 more regional M1 reads with their refusal removed, and the suite stayed green; `MicroQR_M1UnevenLightLowDensity_NotReadByTheRegionalPass` pins it.
- **The failure-path multiple was quoted on an image `main` already paid for**: phase 3b now also names the noisy ramp `main` rejects in 0.2 ms, 80-200x on this branch.
- Set aside, reproduced on `main`: a crisp, evenly lit Standard QR version 1 symbol at exactly 1.95 px/module fails at levels L, M and Q (1.93, 1.94, 1.96 and 1.97 read).

**An eleventh round** kept nine findings after three votes each:
- **A number in the public docs kept needing conditions it did not carry**: after density, anti-aliasing and margin, this round found rotation (a crisp symbol turned at 2 px/module is not read even unlit at some placements) and contrast (every measurement used ink at 30 on paper at 220; ink at 60 on paper at 200 holds to about 37 %, ink at 100 on paper at 170, the low contrast the spec maps list as supported, to about 23 %, no further than `main` at the weakest scales), and "margin" was undefined. The user chose to drop the number from the README and the public decoders' remarks, which now say "a shading gradient or a soft-edged shadow over part of the symbol", and to keep every measured limit in the decoder spec's lighting section, now a list by rendering (crisp along the axes from 2.6 px/module, crisp turned from 3.6, anti-aliased from 4.5 and in all but 3 of about 3,600 turned renders from 3.5) with the contrast, the crop and the placements it was measured under.
- **The candidate stop cost real empty symbols**: an empty symbol read with corrections on its first grid was refused and its candidate ended, so the grid that reads it cleanly was never tried (268-524 renders lost against no stop, 5-19 within the measured limits). Only an M1 read ends the candidate now; the other refusals let the search go on (`MicroQR_EmptySymbolTurnedUnevenLight_ReadByALaterGrid`), with the same cost on M1 (8 and 46-224 grid decodes).
- **The regional pass read other symbologies' texture as M3-M at its correction limit**: 4 in 120,000 turned, shaded Standard QR and rMQR images decoded as Micro QR, digits or letters with 4 of 4 corrections, which `main` does not read (it has its own 6 non-M1 false reads of this class on those images, besides its M1 ones). The regional pass now refuses an M3 or M4 read that needed every correction its level allows (`MicroQR_UnevenLightForeignImage_NoReadAtTheCorrectionLimit`), without ending the candidate; the verifiers measured under 1 % of the pass's Micro QR gain lost that way (2-3 renders within the measured limits, all M2-L, which this rule leaves out).
- **Nothing guarded the candidate stop**: removing it passed the suite. `MicroQRImageEndToEnd.M1_UnderShadow_ImageDecode_Fails` measures that failure path: 24 us, 857 us without the stop.
- **A refused grid's transpose was still decoded** on the fast path; it no longer is, as in the refinement searches.
- Texts: the spec's empty-read sentence (only an empty read that needed correction is refused), the Micro QR spec map's M1 sentence (turned or anti-aliased, as the decoder spec says).

**A twelfth round** kept findings in the spec's lighting numbers, the refusal and its guards:
- **The lighting section's finer numbers were artifacts of one sweep each**: other placements, payloads and margins moved the onsets (anti-aliased at 2 px/module from about 4 % at some sub-pixel placements, not 17; a wide margin losing renders from about 27 % at 2-4 px/module, which the section said the regional pass made up for; low contrast reading no further at 6 px/module, where the section said 43-45 %; M1 anti-aliased from about 17 %). The section now states its measuring conditions first and keeps only the bounds every sweep held to, conservatively, and the Micro QR spec map follows it.
- **A verdict escaped the correction-limit refusal**: the refusal judged reads (`Success`, `DestinationTooSmall`) only, so a grid on another symbology's texture that reached an unmapped Kanji cell at M3-M's limit reported `UnmappedCharacter` (and `NotDetected` into a one-character destination), where `main` reports `NotDetected`. Verdicts are judged like reads now (`MicroQR_UnevenLightForeignImage_NoVerdictAtTheCorrectionLimit`); a real unmapped symbol at its limit under a shadow gives `DataUncorrectable`, as a mappable one already did.
- **The refinement searches' stop and the rule's edges had no guard**: dropping the stop in the rotation, scale and perspective searches turned a turned M1 failure from 1.5 ms into 7.6 ms with the suite green, now measured by `MicroQRImageEndToEnd.M1_TurnedUnderShadow_ImageDecode_Fails`; widening the rule to M2, to one correction short of the limit, or to short destinations passed too, now pinned by `MicroQR_DamagedUnevenLight_ReadByTheRegionalPass` (M2-L at its limit, M3-L and M4-L one short, each into a short destination). The foreign-image test asserts its premise: without the refusal those images read at the limit.
- **The refusal's cost was quoted from a wider rule**: the shipped rules cost no read within the lighting bounds, and past them, under deeper shadows, up to about 2 % of the Micro QR gain (the correction-limit rule alone 0.3 %, the empty-read rule about 1 % with one payload in four empty).
- Texts: two comments that said every refusal ends the candidate (only M1 does).

**A thirteenth round** kept three findings:
- **The correction-limit rule cost real M4 reads within the lighting bounds**: an M4 symbol that sampling already put at its limit (3 of 3 on M4-L, 5 of 5 on M4-M) at one turned placement was refused, 1 or 2 renders in 10,000 crisp or anti-aliased at 40 %, and the same for an unmapped Kanji verdict. Every false read at a limit the regional pass added was an M3-M (a random word falls within its 4 corrections at least 14 times as often as for any other level, and one M3-L symbol was lost at its limit too), so the rule was narrowed to M3-M, then widened to M4-M once a verifier found one M4-M false verdict at 5 of 5 corrections in 150,000 foreign images (`MicroQR_UnevenLightForeignImage_NoVerdictAtTheCorrectionLimit` gained it); every foreign-image guard holds. `MicroQR_DamagedUnevenLight_ReadByTheRegionalPass` gained an M4-L and an M3-L symbol at their limits (each red under the wider rule).
- **The turned bounds were 2 points high for one family**: Standard QR version 1 (mostly Q and H) turned near 45° with the light along the diagonal loses up to about 1 render in 200 from 38 %, crisp from 3.6 px/module and anti-aliased from 4.5, and from 36 % once the margin is 2 modules wider than the quiet zone. The spec's turned and margin bullets say so.
- **A one-character read's refusal edge had no test**: widening the empty-read refusal to one character passed the suite; the damaged-symbol test now has a one-character M3-L symbol that needed a correction.

**A fourteenth round** kept seven findings:
- **A false verdict from the global threshold hid a readable symbol**: an M3-M or M4-M "12345" under a 40 % shadow at one turned placement gave the global attempt an `UnmappedCharacter` at M3-M's limit of 4, which skipped the regional pass that reads it cleanly; `main` reports `DataUncorrectable` there. A Micro QR verdict at level M's correction limit no longer skips the regional pass: a read there is reported, otherwise the verdict (`MicroQR_GlobalVerdictAtTheCorrectionLimit_RegionalPassReads`, and `MicroQR_UnmappedCellAtTheCorrectionLimit_ReachesTheCallerAsUnmappedCharacter` for a real M4-M verdict at its limit).
- **The M4-M limit rule has a cost**: about 1 in 15,000 anti-aliased M4-M renders at 3.5-4.5 px/module under a 40 % shadow, none measured crisp or from 4.5. The spec states it.
- **Lighting text**: anti-aliased Micro QR M4 turned near 220-225° with the light toward 45° loses a few renders in a thousand at 40 %; low contrast holds to about 30 % (60/200) and 17 % (100/170), with a few turned renders in a thousand lost beyond; the deeper-shadow sentence is scoped to whole pixels along the axes; the sentence comparing with `main` is gone.
- Texts: the damaged-symbol test's summary (M4-L, not M4, at its limit), the Micro QR benchmark summary (it measures decode too).

After this round the user asked for comments to be written only once the behavior is confirmed, without plan markers, and tersely; the branch's comments and test summaries were cut to that.

The fourteenth round's last code findings (false results at M3-L's and M2-M's limit, false verdicts from the global attempt, the M4-M rule's loss at a crisp placement, the rule's untested edges at M2-M, M3-M one short and M4-Q) were verified only in part and are not fixed on this branch: they share one cause and go to phase 3c.

### Phase 3b: the failure path does the same work once (2026-09-24)

**Done.** Measured first, on `main` at 76ac1cb: the sweep and the corpus as the baseline, and a failing decode profiled on 512 × 512 noise-like images. rMQR spent 87 % of it in `TryLocateSubFinder`; Micro QR spent 90 % in the scale and perspective searches, of which sampling the grid 32 %, codeword extraction 27 %, Reed-Solomon 13 %, the format read 9 % and the transpose for the mirrored read 5 %. Three changes, each a structure rather than a tuning, each bit-identical in result:

- **rMQR: the sub-finder search screens its positions on the lattice they share.** A position (ou, ov) samples the half-module lattice points (ou + 2i, ov + 2j), so each point served up to 25 positions and was read once per position. The lattice is now classified once per lean (dark, light, outside, or next to a pixel edge), and a position with two certain mismatches, which cannot reach the 24 of 25 the template needs, is dropped with all the positions of its row at once in 64-bit masks; the first three rings are scored as before, since a sub-finder near its prediction is found before the screen pays for itself. The screen's float expression is not the search's, so a point within a margin of a pixel edge or the border counts as a match either way; the margin is 2^-18 of the largest coordinate either expression forms, several times their rounding. With it, the ring walk no longer visits each ring's interior (it had been O(r³) iterations, invisible while scoring dominated), and the classification has a 128-bit tier and a branch-free pixel read (on texture the class is a coin toss, and the branch mispredicted half the time: that alone was 1.5x).
- **Micro QR: each grid is sampled once and read in both orientations.** The mirrored read goes through a view that transposes the module index instead of a transposed copy, codewords come through a placement table per size (built from the encoder's own function-module and mask predicates) instead of testing both per module, the affine sampler has a 128-bit tier (lane for lane the scalar arithmetic, as the Standard QR sampler's), and the format word is looked up in a 32 KB table of the words within 3 bits of each candidate (the balls never overlap, so the table is the search).
- **Both: the full sweep does not decode a candidate the strided scan already decoded.** A candidate's decode reads its position and module size, the image, the threshold and, for Micro QR, the refusal rule, and the scan's best failure only once that is terminal; so a candidate the strided scan tried without settling settles on nothing in the sweep either, and skipping it changes only a failure the caller does not report. The sweep still tries its own first eight: a skipped one is not replaced by the ninth. When the strided scan settled (a verdict on the content), nothing is skipped. The plan expected 10-20 % here; on Micro QR it was most of the lever, because the sweep's top eight on texture are largely the strided scan's.

Tests: `RmQRSubFinderScreenParityTest` (56 a framework): the search against the unscreened search transcribed, bit for bit over 1,440 frames (turned and keystoned symbols, symbols framed off, symbols 10,000 to 20,000 px out on a wide image, two-level and 8-bit noise); every dropped position scoring under the floor when sampled the search's way; every certain lattice point the pixel the search reads, on a one-pixel checkerboard 16,000 to 32,768 px out (setting the margin to 0 fails it; dropping at one mismatch instead of two fails the drop test); vector against scalar classification; most positions dropped on noise; a lattice wider than a mask refused. `MicroQRGridReadParityTest` (49 a framework): the matrix decode against the whole-matrix extraction transcribed, over real, damaged and random-under-a-valid-format matrices (status, diagnostics, characters written and the whole destination); the transposed view against a transposed copy (a view that does not swap fails 16); vector against scalar affine sampling, frames off the image included; the format table against the search for all 65,536 words. `ContentVerdictImageDecodeTest.TwoUnmappedSymbols_TheSweepReportsTheOneTheStridedScanFound` (Micro QR, rMQR) holds the skip's one exception: a strided scan that settled on a verdict leaves the sweep every candidate, and without that the sweep reports a second unmapped symbol only it finds instead of the first; it passes on `main` and fails with the exception removed.

**Exit met.** Sweep and corpus against `main`, image for image: Standard QR 54,400, Micro QR 18,400, rMQR 29,440 and the 624 corpus reads identical in every FeatherQR status (the result files differ in one line, zxing-cpp's verdict on one Standard QR render, a code path this phase does not touch). Full suite green on both frameworks (28,057; 378 skipped on this x64 machine). Failing decodes, fastest of interleaved runs, `main` → this phase, ms:

| Image (512 × 512 unless named) | Micro QR | rMQR | Standard QR |
|---|---|---|---|
| two-level noise, 1 px | 91.7 → 47.6 (1.9x) | 119 → 16.8 (7.1x) | 0.94 → 0.91 |
| two-level noise, 2 px | 60.3 → 25.7 (2.3x) | 56.1 → 7.7 (7.3x) | 0.71 → 0.69 |
| 8-bit noise | 200 → 108 (1.9x) | 253 → 40.1 (6.3x) | 2.46 → 2.40 |
| ramp ±20 noise, 256 px | 28.3 → 10.9 (2.6x) | 18.2 → 2.76 (6.6x) | 0.22 → 0.21 |
| ramp ±20 noise | 36.4 → 17.4 (2.1x) | 48.3 → 6.69 (7.2x) | 1.36 → 1.37 |
| ramp ±40 noise (textured) | 17.6 → 11.4 (1.5x) | 29.1 → 6.05 (4.8x) | 1.37 → 1.34 |
| blurred noise, plain ramp | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged |
| Standard QR v10 at 4 px | 77.6 → 31.2 (2.5x) | 11.9 → 3.66 (3.3x) | (reads) |
| Micro QR M4, turned / keystoned | (reads) | 2.70 → 1.31, 2.31 → 1.19 | |
| rMQR R13x139 turned / keystoned, R7x43 turned | 30.9 → 14.2, 25.9 → 7.9, 32.6 → 18.5 | (reads) | |

Per lever, on 8-bit noise: the rMQR screen alone 2.0x, with the ring walk 2.6x, the vector classification 3.5x, the branch-free read 5.4x; the Micro QR grid path alone 1.6x (1.5-1.7x over the images above); the sweep skip then took Micro QR to 1.9x and rMQR to 6.3x. The kernels against the end to end: `TryLocateSubFinder` 221 → 17 ms a decode (13x) for 6.3x; Micro QR sampling, extraction, transpose and format 132 → 46 ms (2.9x) for 1.9x.

**Refuted, with the numbers.**

- **Micro QR modules read on demand through the transform**, format first and data in placement order, no grid sampled whole: 1.2x. Both orientations read their data modules (about 190 each), more than the 289 of one whole-grid sample, and each read paid the float work of a sample. Replaced by one vector sample read through a transposing view.
- **Remembering grids already decoded** within a candidate's search: 523 of 197,432 grids on 8-bit noise repeated the one before and 993 any earlier one of the same candidate; 19 % on a Standard QR image. Not built.
- **Stopping Reed-Solomon once the error locator's degree passes Micro QR's capacity**: not bit-identical. A block the capacity cap rejects reports its corrected-error count in the diagnostics, and only the full correction computes it.

**Lessons.** A search over positions that share their samples is a search over the samples: the 2,601 positions of a lean on the widest symbol read the same 3,481 lattice points up to 25 times each, and once the points are read once, scoring every position is a handful of mask operations. The exactness came from a margin, not from reproducing the float expression: two expressions of the same point differ by a few roundings, and a point near a pixel edge simply says nothing. Removing the dominant cost exposed two that had been hidden under it and that no profile of the old code showed: a ring walk that visited every ring's interior, and a pixel branch that texture mispredicts half the time. And a module read on demand is only cheaper when fewer modules are read: two orientations of one grid read more of it than sampling it once, so the cut that worked was the transpose, not the sample.

**Benchmark delta.** Success paths unchanged (ShortRun, fastest of two interleaved rounds, `main` → this phase): `M4_ImageDecode_Span` 5.03 → 4.70 µs, `R7x43_ImageDecode_Span` 5.39 → 5.29 µs, `R17x139_ImageDecode_Span` 20.3 → 19.5 µs, `R7x43_BitmapDecode` 7.56 → 7.68 µs, `R17x139_BitmapDecode` 31.2 → 29.7 µs, allocations unchanged. Failure paths: `NoSymbol_Noise_1144x168` 6,829 → 885 µs (7.7x), `M1_TurnedUnderShadow_ImageDecode_Fails` 912 → 547 µs, `M1_UnderShadow_ImageDecode_Fails` 21.1 → 20.7 µs, `NoSymbol_Gradient_1144x168` 276 → 283 µs (within its error).

### Phase 3c: every grid earns its corrections (2026-09-24)

**Measured first.** A probe (scratchpad, not committed) rendered 1,000,000 foreign images, 70 % Standard QR and 30 % rMQR at 1.8-4 px/module, axis-aligned or turned, crisp or anti-aliased, evenly lit or under a ramp or shadow of 20-50 %, half of them negated, and decoded each as Micro QR, image for image on three trees:

| Tree | False reads | False verdicts |
|---|---|---|
| `main` before phase 3 (9707a1e) | 1,110: 1,088 M1, 19 M3-M at 4, 2 M3-L at 2, 1 M2-M at 2 | 0 |
| `main` after phase 3b (099292e) | 1,112, the same classes | 25: 20 M3-M, 3 M3-L, 2 M4-M, each at its limit |
| This phase | 1 (M3-L at 2) | 1 (M3-L at 2) |

`main`'s own false reads were far more common than the review rounds had found (about 1 in 1,000 images, most of them M1, evenly lit ones included), and every non-M1 one sat exactly at its level's limit. Instrumenting the decoder over 20,000 of those images explained both: each failing image sends about 19,000 grids through Reed-Solomon, and a random word passes a level with `e` corrections with probability `V(n, e) / 256^ecc`, which in bits is M1 16, M3-M at 4 20.8, M4-M at 5 24.7, M3-L at 2 24.9, M2-M at 2 26.5, M2-L 28.7, M4-L 29.0 and M4-Q at 7 37.6: the order in which the review rounds kept finding false results. On those grids the format distance fell exactly where the combinatorics put it (0 bits off: 9.6e-4 measured, 9.8e-4 predicted; at most 1: 1.57 % and 1.56 %), the timing modules matched no better than even odds, and the quiet-zone line was light far more often than random (the grid hangs over a margin) except given a clean timing line, where it is close to one dark module in three. Finder and separator are no evidence at all: a Standard QR finder and its separator are a Micro QR's.

**Done.** `MicroQRGridEvidence` replaces the regional pass's refusals by level (M1, an empty read that needed correction, M3-M and M4-M at their limit, the global verdict at level M's limit that retried the regional pass) and the M1 stop of a candidate's search with one rule in every pass: a sampled grid's read is kept when the bits of Reed-Solomon at its correction count, of the format word (the share of the 576 words within 3 bits of a candidate that lie within its distance), of the timing modules (the binomial tail of their mismatches at even odds) and, where those fall short, of the quiet-zone line next to the symbol (its dark count's tail at 0.3) add up to 33, which leaves about 2^-19 an image at 2^14 grids before the bitstream's own validity. A symbol that shows its structure uses every correction its level allows; M1, which corrects nothing, is never kept on its format and timing alone. The structure is counted only after Reed-Solomon reads a grid, and the quiet zone last, through a sampler each search hands the decode (affine, projective, or counted on the module-boundary grids), so texture that fails correction costs nothing more. The format table now carries each word's distance in the same byte. The matrix API is not held to the rule.

Tests: `MicroQRGridEvidenceTest` (27 a framework): the table against the exact sum for every level, format distance, timing count and quiet-zone count; a clean grid uses every correction; M1 needs its quiet zone; texture-like structure keeps fewer corrections at each level; a real M4-M symbol at its limit with its structure damaged fails, reads once its quiet zone earns the difference and with the rule suspended, mirrored too; the matrix path is not held to the rule. `UnevenLightingDecodeTest`: M1 read by the regional pass (both polarities, a short destination, module-boundary grids at 1-1.25 px/module), M3-M and M4-M at their limits read, two evenly lit Standard QR images `main` read as M1 not read, two real M1 symbols the branch misread now read correctly, and the verdict at the limit gone; each refusal test asserts through `MicroQRGridEvidence.SuspendedOnThisThread` that without the rule the image is read. Mutations: `Earns` always true fails 21 tests, the quiet zone never read fails 10. `MicroQRGridReadParityTest` checks the folded distance for every 16-bit word. Full suite green on both frameworks.

**Exit.** Foreign sweep: 1,110 → 2 against `main` before phase 3 (reads 1,110 → 1; verdicts 0 → 1, of which `main` after phase 3 had 25): both residuals are M3-L at its limit on rMQR images, the one traced reaching 35.0 bits with its timing 1 of 14 off and its format 3 bits off, the rate the threshold is set for; a stricter threshold is the trade below. `main`'s own M1 false reads: 1,088 → 0. Real reads, against this branch before the phase:

- 200,000 renders, M1-M4 at 1.5-6 px/module, a random turn, crisp or anti-aliased, evenly lit, a ramp to 80 % or a shadow to 50 %, 15 % negated: 186,962 → 194,520 (+7,570, −12), misreads 19 → 3. Every loss is M1 at 1.5-2.1 px/module, most anti-aliased; one is evenly lit and one under a 16 % shadow, the rest past the lighting bounds.
- M1 under the spec's own lighting conditions (a 40 % shadow, renders that read evenly lit): crisp along the axes from 2.6 px/module 3,265 → 9,987 of 10,000, crisp turned from 3.6 101 → 9,996, anti-aliased from 3.5 0 → 9,998. M1 now holds the bounds M2-M4 hold; the decoder spec says so.
- 200,000 evenly lit renders at 1-2.5 px/module, anti-aliased or a bilinear upscale: M1 43,442 → 43,189 (−256, +3), M2-M4 126,432 → 126,417; misreads 38 → 17.
- The sweep tool: Micro QR +24 (bilinear at 2-2.5 px/module) and −10 (five M1 images at 1.2-2.0 px/module, each from two encoders); the corpus identical image for image.

**Against the other readers.** The two references in `.references/` that decode Micro QR, zxing-cpp (0.5.2, `TryHarder`) and CodeGlyphX (2.1.0, RGBA input), on the same images:

| Set | This library | zxing-cpp | CodeGlyphX |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,000,000 foreign images, false reads | 1 | 274 | 2,306 |
| 200,000 mixed real renders, read / misread | 194,520 / 3 | 166,280 / 18 | 148,116 / 853 |
| 200,000 evenly lit at 1-2.5 px/module, read / misread | 169,606 / 17 | 54,397 / 64 | 62,817 / 1,214 |
| M1 under a 40 % shadow (crisp axes, crisp turned, anti-aliased) | 9,987, 9,996, 9,998 of 10,000 | 9,821, 9,936, 9,890 | 3,237, 100, 0 |

The designs explain the rows. zxing-cpp samples one grid a finder (the best of four orientations by format distance), checks two timing modules and rejects only a quiet zone more than two-thirds dark, and corrects at Reed-Solomon's full strength, past the misdecode-protection cap: few grids keep its false reads low and cost it reads. CodeGlyphX checks finder, separator and timing modules against fixed budgets whatever the correction count, which a Standard QR corner passes. Renders zxing-cpp reads and this library does not: 1,102 mixed and 1,922 at low density, of which this phase lost 2 and 28; the rest were unread before it and belong to phases 4 and 7.

**Refuted, with the numbers.**

- **The quiet zone's second ring** (1.5 modules out, clear of the grey an anti-aliased edge leaves): low-density M1 losses 256 → 63 and M2-M4 15 → 0, but near-miss misreads 17 → 21, the two real M1 misreads back and an M4-M foreign verdict back. A grid a little too small puts the first ring on the symbol's own edge; the second ring cannot see that. Both rings together: losses 34, misreads 28.
- **The worse of the two timing lines, counted twice**, on the reading that rMQR's top-edge timing pattern lent the residual verdict its row 0: the verdict stayed and low-density M1 losses doubled. The trace, not the reasoning, found the cause.
- **The threshold.** Low-density M1 losses and misreads at 29: 77 and 25; 31: 174 and 20; 33: 274 and 16; 35: 516 and 11 (measured before the quiet zone moved to its final sampler); the predicted foreign false results fall from 7.7 to 0.3 a million over the same range. 33 is where both are small; 36 excludes the traced verdict and, measured with the second ring, lost 21 of the 200,000 mixed renders where 33 lost 8.
- **A check before Reed-Solomon**, as this phase was worded: it saves nothing. M2-M4's Reed-Solomon bits at zero corrections already reach 33, so no grid could be refused before it, and M1's correction is cheaper than reading 23 quiet-zone pixels; that order was 8 % slower on noise than `main`. The structure is counted after a read instead.
- **Near-miss M1 grids by re-sampling nudged grids** from the kept read's corners: the corner transform is not faithful at 1-2 px/module (real reads came out as unstable as the misreads), so it measured nothing.

**Left.** M1 misreads at low density: 17 in 200,000 renders at 1-2.5 px/module (38 before), each a grid near the real symbol whose finder, timing, format and quiet zone are right and whose data is mis-sampled in 3 or more codewords, which M1's 16 bits of detection pass one time in 65,536 across the thousands of grids a hard render gets. No structure tells those grids from the real one; it needs a check on the data (the same codewords from a second grid) or a bound on the grids a candidate may try, and belongs with phase 4, where those densities are the subject. The two foreign residuals are both rMQR images at M3-L's limit; two images do not make a cause.

**Lessons.** A refusal by level is a threshold on one term of a sum: each one cost real reads and left the next level texture landed on, because what decides is the sum. Structure another symbology shares is no evidence: a Standard QR corner has a Micro QR's finder and separator, so only the timing modules and the quiet zone count. Texture and a near-miss grid of the real symbol are different adversaries: structure beats texture, only the ring next to the symbol sees a near-miss, and a change that helps against one can arm the other, so each has its own measuring set. Place a check where it is cheap, not where the pipeline draws it: the plan said before Reed-Solomon, and after it is where the check costs nothing. And the first "faster" number this phase produced (a 50,000-render run taking 7.8 s against 10.7) was other runs on the machine: timings come from interleaved rounds with nothing else running.

**Benchmark delta.** `main` (099292e) → this phase, fastest of interleaved rounds on an otherwise idle machine, single thread: failing decodes at 512 × 512, two-level noise 1 px 21.4 → 21.0 ms, 2 px 30.0 → 30.3 ms, 8-bit noise 111 → 109 ms, ramps with ±20 and ±40 noise 64.6 → 64.7 ms and 54.9 → 55.2 ms; a Standard QR version 10 image at 4 px/module 13.0 → 13.2 ms, a turned rMQR 10.6 → 10.6 ms. BenchmarkDotNet (ShortRun, two rounds): `M4_ImageDecode_Span` 4.77-4.84 → 4.86-5.04 µs (within its error), `StandardQRImage_ImageDecode_Fails` (new) 13.1-13.2 → 13.5-13.7 ms (within its error), `M1_UnderShadow_ImageDecode` 20.1-21.4 → 12.6-12.7 µs (it reads now), `M1_TurnedUnderShadow_ImageDecode_Fails` 0.53-0.54 → 2.58-2.60 ms: a 55 % shadow on a turned anti-aliased symbol, past the bounds, where the old refusal ended the candidate's search at its first M1 grid and a pass that reads M1 has to search it.

### Phase 4: the frame from grey levels, a second reading by coverage (2026-09-25)

**Measured first.** The baseline sweep and corpus reproduced on `main` at fb6479c (qrtool was not located on this machine, so Standard QR is six encoders, 2,400 renders a kind). The diagnosis column the plan asked for, a probe that sampled each render of the failing kinds through the geometry it was drawn with: with the decoder's own reader (one pixel against Otsu) anti-aliased renders at 1.25-1.5 px/module read 2,388 of 2,400 where the decoder read 1,367, 1,021 of its 1,033 failures; bilinear upscales at 1.5-2 read 2,338 where it read 1,894. The failures were in the frame, and a second column said where: the finders the decoder found were a median 0.22 modules off and up to half a module, and the parallelogram through them extrapolated that across the symbol. What was left through the true frame was the pixel: the luminance interpolated at the module centre against the midpoint of the two levels read 2,399 of the bilinear renders where one pixel against Otsu read 2,338. Micro QR and rMQR said the same (Micro QR bilinear 1.5-2: 48 of 51 failures read through the true frame, rMQR 85 of 85, anti-aliased 1.25-1.5 135 of 135), with one more class: Micro QR bilinear at 2.44-2.50 px/module was `NotDetected`, no finder candidate at all.

zxing-cpp gets its centres by tracing the rings' edges on a binarized image and averaging the edge points (`LocateConcentricPattern`, `FindConcentricPatternCorners`), which averages the quantization over many edge points. The grey levels this decoder already takes for the finder's second look carry the sub-pixel positions directly, so the design uses them instead.

**Done.** Four pieces, each for a class the diagnosis named, the first two shared by all three decoders:

- `ConcentricCentroid`: a concentric pattern's centre as the darkness-weighted centroid of its centre square, in a window along the symbol's axes that ends inside the light ring, two passes, integer darkness from whole levels so the sums are exact in any order. It refines the three Standard QR finders (window scaled by each finder's own module size along the finder-to-finder lines), the alignment patterns and mesh nodes, the Micro QR finder and the rMQR finder and sub-finder; the module size the Standard QR dimension estimate divides by is measured again from the refined centres. Only on an image with grey levels.
- The coverage reading (`LuminanceSampler`): a grid that failed on an image with grey levels is read again, each module's interpolated luminance against the midpoint of the two levels, and decoded only when a module changed. Standard QR reads its global grid again, rMQR a grid that read its format information, Micro QR a grid whose format word read exactly.
- Standard QR's dimension from the timing modules: the grid of each dimension within four versions of the estimate is sampled along both timing lines through the refined finders, and the one with under an eighth of them wrong is tried, where the estimate is refused and the count fails, and after the version information when the estimate's grid fails.
- Micro QR and rMQR scan for finders once more at the midpoint of the two levels when both scans found no candidate on an image with grey levels.

The reasons and the measurements behind each are lessons in [standardqr-decoder.md](../specs/standardqr-decoder.md) (image detection), and the envelopes of the three decoders say 1.5 px/module for grey edges.

Tests: `SubPixelFrameDecodeTest` (31 a framework, every render red on `main`): Standard QR anti-aliased at 1.26 px/module (versions 12-36), bilinear upscales (versions 2-6), version 40 and an estimate a version out at 30 and 36 whose dimension only the timing match gives, Micro QR and rMQR anti-aliased and bilinear, and the blurred finder at 2.51-2.54 px/module with its premise asserted (no candidate at the global threshold, one at the midpoint). Each group fails with its own mechanism removed: without the centroid 9, without the coverage reading 15, without the midpoint scan 4, without the timing match 4. `ConcentricCentroidTest` (44): within a tenth of a module from a start half a pixel off at 1.25-3.7 px/module and turned, and each refusal (two-level image, a dark area of 16 or 1 modules where 9 is expected, a shift past the bound), each failing with its bound removed; one pass instead of two fails 11 placements. `LuminanceSamplerTest` (15): exact at pixel centres, weighted between them, edge pixels past the border, the midpoint half dark. `BilinearUpscaleRenderer` is a C# upscale with Skia's mapping, so the tests do not depend on a resampler's version. **Refuted, with the numbers.**

- **The whole finder as the centroid's window** (± 4 modules, the dark ring's edges averaged in): a median 0.073 modules against 0.044, and 2,096 of 2,400 reads against 2,261 at 1.25-1.5 px/module.
- **Linear darkness from the image's extremes** instead of the class levels: 0.043 against 0.044. The levels are not what limits it.
- **The dark area as the module size** (√(area / 9)): within 2 % on anti-aliased renders, 2 % high on bilinear ones and 15 % either way on crisp ones, where a square drawn in whole pixels is not 9 modules.
- **One pass**: 11 of 36 placements more than a tenth of a module off below 1.6 px/module.

- **Micro QR's coverage reading after every grid past its format information**: 8-bit noise 1.78x and other symbologies' images 2-5.6x. Keeping it out of the scale and perspective searches instead lost 34 bilinear and 17 anti-aliased reads at 1.25-2 px/module. And without the refined centre in the arbitrary-orientation search Micro QR bilinear 1.5-2 fell 798 → 761.
- **The midpoint scan gated on a status** (no grid read format information): it ran on every other symbology's image, rMQR on a Micro QR image up to 2.9x.

**Checked on the final code.** Foreign images decoded as Micro QR, 1,000,000 (the evidence phase's set): the same 2 false results on `main` and on this phase, the same two images (M3-L at its limit on rMQR images). Micro QR evenly lit at 1-2.5 px/module, anti-aliased or a bilinear upscale, 194,949 renders: 168,618 → 183,068 read, misreads 11 → 3 (all M1). The mixed set (200,000: M1-M4 at 1.5-6 px/module, any turn, ramps and shadows, 15 % negated): 194,520 → 194,560 read, misreads 3 → 5, all M1 with nothing corrected; one of `main`'s is read now and three that `main` read are misread (at 1.63, 1.66 and 4.29 px/module under 19-20 % shadows). The centroid is not biased on those three (0.04-0.08 modules from the true centre, closer than the run centre in two), and with it switched off each reads: they are the near-miss grids the evidence phase left here, whose structure is the real symbol's and whose data M1's 16 bits of detection pass one time in 65,536; a different starting point changes which grids the search tries, and so which such grid gets through. Over the two sets the M1 misreads went 14 → 8.

**Left.** M1 near-miss misreads: 8 in about 395,000 renders, and a read of any M1 symbol is still one grid that passes 16 bits. What would fix them as a class is a check on the data, not the structure: an M1 read kept only when a second grid, the frame nudged by a fraction of a module, reads the same codewords (a real symbol's read is stable under the nudge; a grid that passed by chance is not). Its own measurement and the foreign set; it is the next item for Micro QR, not taken here. Out of this phase: keystone past 6 % (Standard QR phase 5, rMQR phase 7), where refining binarized images is the lead measured above; anti-aliased input under 1.25 px/module, which moved (Standard QR 36 → 343 of 2,400) but stays out of scope; the corner accuracy the public docs state was not re-measured now that the alignment centre is refined on grey images.

**Lessons.** The plan's candidates for this phase were all about the pixels (a midpoint threshold, a module's footprint mean, a threshold local to the symbol, a 2x resample), and the first measurement, the true-transform column, said the frame: one afternoon of diagnosis decided which mechanism to build before any was built. Each mechanism then needed tests that fail without it: renders chosen as "red on `main`, green now" did not tell the centroid from the coverage reading, because on many renders either one alone reads, so the cases were chosen again per mechanism with each switched off. A gate on a failure-path retry has to be measured in the unit the cost is paid in, grids: "a grid got past its format information" was rare on the renders the retry was for and half of all grids on texture. Where a fallback sits in the order decides who pays for it: inside each attempt the midpoint scan charged every symbol the regional pass reads, at the end only the images nothing else reads. And the tests that assert their premises paid off: when the refined centre stopped a near-miss grid being sampled first, the evidence-rule tests failed on their premise instead of passing while guarding nothing.

**Benchmark delta.** BenchmarkDotNet in process, final code, one round a tree back to back on a quiet machine (`main` → this phase; `main`'s three rounds span up to 12 %, so the same round is the comparison): Standard QR `v40-3px` 89.4 → 89.5 µs, `v40-3.4px` 100.1 → 102.4, `v40-4px-rot17` 274.5 → 291.5 (+6.2 %), `v40-4px-soft` 253.6 → 267.0 (+5.3 %), `v6-4px` 9.55 → 9.59, `none-noise` 3,173 → 3,209, `none-gradient` 778 → 776; Micro QR `M4_ImageDecode_Span` 4.33 → 4.37, `M1_UnderShadow_ImageDecode` 11.52 → 11.54, `M1_TurnedUnderShadow_ImageDecode_Fails` 2,443 → 2,493, `StandardQRImage_ImageDecode_Fails` 12,940 → 12,991; rMQR `R7x43_ImageDecode_Span` 4.98 → 5.00, `R17x139_ImageDecode_Span` 19.19 → 19.27, `NoSymbol_Noise_1144x168` 913 → 912, `NoSymbol_Gradient_1144x168` 284 → 293 (+3.3 %, two midpoint sweeps on an image with no finder at all). The two grey-image v40 reads are the success-path cost of the refined frame. Before the midpoint scan moved behind the regional pass, `M1_UnderShadow_ImageDecode` was +24 % (11.25 → 13.98 µs). Failing decodes at 512 × 512, fastest of interleaved rounds (x `main`): Standard QR 8-bit noise 1.08, a damaged anti-aliased v10 1.33 (its grid read again by coverage), two-level noise and ramps within 5 %; Micro QR 8-bit noise 1.04, Standard QR images 1.03-1.25, an rMQR image 2.3 (the refined centre makes the searches on rMQR's identical finder go deeper: 0.75 → 1.7 ms), a damaged Micro QR 1.65; rMQR 8-bit noise 1.21, Standard QR images 0.97-1.25, a damaged Micro QR image 1.04 once the midpoint scan was gated on candidates (2.98 before). ### Phase 5: the finders' frame (2026-09-25)

**Measured first.** The baseline reproduced on `main` at fa669d0 (six encoders; qrtool is not on this machine): keystone 6-20 % read 2,210 of 2,400, the gap 190, by version band v1 47 of 60 renders failing, v2-13 none, v14-20 5, v21-30 48, v31-40 90. The true-transform column, for the 32 of 400 cases that failed with this library's own symbol: every one read through the geometry it was drawn with, by one pixel against Otsu and by coverage, and the finder centres were refined to within a tenth of a module. So the frame, and three ways of it:

- **Versions 21-40: the bottom-right alignment pattern was searched in the wrong place.** The parallelogram of the three centres predicted it 17 to 30 modules off at versions 31-40 (median 17, 12 at 21-30), the widening window (4, 8, 16 modules) anchored on the pattern one lattice step in (24 to 28 modules off), and the mesh, seeded from the same parallelogram, found 0 to 2 of its 16 to 36 nodes in all but two of them.
- **Version 1: nothing to anchor.** The parallelogram grid missed its far corner by 0.9 to 2.0 modules.
- **The dimension estimate a version off** in 7 of the 24 large cases, which the timing count and the version information corrected; not a cause on its own.

zxing-cpp gets the same corner by intersecting regression lines fitted to the finders' ring edges (the inner and outer edge of the side facing the top-left finder, seven modules long, extrapolated across the symbol), searches the alignment pattern at nine points 2.8 modules apart around it, reads the version through that transform, predicts the rest of the lattice from it, and samples each lattice cell through its own four-point transform. It also tries up to 256 finder triples in turn.

The finders already say how far the symbol is from flat: along each finder line a plane in perspective changes the module size, the size at one end over the size at the other is the square of the ratio of the two ends' projective weights, and the three centres with the four sizes at the ends of the two lines fix the plane. With true sizes that frame predicted the alignment pattern within 0.15 module at every version; with the sizes the decoder measured it was as good as the measurement, so the measurement was tested next (400 keystoned renders, prediction error at versions 31-40, median / 90th percentile / worst, in modules):

| Sizes | Size error, median / worst | Prediction |
|---|---|---|
| The parallelogram (no sizes) | | 17.5 / 25.2 / 30.4 |
| Whole-pixel runs (`MeasureAxis`) | 2 % / 7 % | 1.8 / 4.0 / 8.0 |
| Darkness integrated along the line | 1.3 % / 5 % | 1.1 / 2.4 / 6.5 |
| Midpoint crossings of the luminance interpolated along the line | 0.5 % / 2 % | 0.47 / 0.89 / 2.0 |
| True sizes | | 0.01 / 0.05 / 0.11 |

**Done.** `QRImageDecoder.FinderFrame`, and four uses of it:

- The frame: `((1 − a − b)·TL + w_u·a·TR + w_v·b·BL) / ((1 − a − b) + w_u·a + w_v·b)` with `w = √(s_near / s_far)` on each line, the parallelogram when both weights are 1, and refused (the parallelogram) when the weights would put the vanishing line across the symbol.
- The sizes: whole-pixel runs as before for the centre refinement, then, on an image with grey levels, again from the refined centres to midpoint crossings (`FinderAxisEstimator.MeasureAxisAtLevel`, half-pixel steps). On a binarized image the runs are all there is, and a line takes the change they show only past their resolution: their sizes are whole twelfths of a pixel, each within two twelfths, so two ends that differ by up to four twelfths are one size.
- The bottom-right alignment pattern is searched where the frame puts it, with the grid axes the frame has there (a keystone turns and scales them away from the ones at the finders, and the ring check samples along them).
- Where nothing anchors the fourth corner (version 1, or no alignment pattern found), the parallelogram is sampled first as before and the frame second, read again by coverage on grey images; and the timing match samples the timing patterns through the frame.

Tests: `FinderFrameTest` (27 a framework): the frame against twelve planes, every module centre within a hundredth of a module where the parallelogram is a module or more off; equal sizes bit for bit the parallelogram; the horizon refusal at weights 0.55 and not at 0.62; the runs' bound at 52 and 53 twelfths; the timing match through the frame naming the dimension the parallelogram misses (versions 20-40 at 30-45 %, finders placed where the render drew them); the alignment search anchoring on the right pattern where the parallelogram's does not; the four sizes sub-pixel and within 2 % on grey edges, along the axes and turned. `FinderAxisSubPixelTest` (6): midpoint crossings within 2 % of the drawn size at 2.3-4.6 px/module where whole-pixel runs miss that bound; a walk leaving the image or starting on light is NaN. `KeystoneFrameDecodeTest` (30): versions 25-40 at 20 % keystone, version 1 at 15-20 %, two binarized renders, each with its four corners within half a module of the drawn ones; a keystoned version 1 with its data destroyed does not decode; and five of zxing-cpp's real images at the four right angles (`qrcode-3/09`, `/21`, `/23`, `qrcode-2/estimate-tilt.jpg`, `low-res-v1-a.webp`). Every render in them was chosen from a search to hold under nudges (turn ±0.5°, density ±0.02, keystone ±0.005) and to fail without its mechanism. `QRCodeDecoderPerspectiveTest` keeps its cases, adds version 1 at 10 and 16 % keystone, versions 10 and 25 at 20 % and version 40 at 16 %, and no longer calls version 1's limit 2 % by design. Red checks, each mechanism switched off alone on this code: the prediction at the frame (large versions, `qrcode-3/09` at 0° and 270°, `/21`, `/23`, one binarized render, the alignment-search unit tests), the grid axes there (`qrcode-3/09` at 0° and 270°, `/21`, `/23`), the frame as the last grid (version 1, the binarized version 1, `estimate-tilt.jpg`, `low-res-v1-a.webp`), the timing match (its unit tests), the sub-pixel sizes (a version 1 render, and the accuracy test on the function), the runs' bound (its unit test and the binarized version 1) and runs weighing binarized images at all (both binarized renders, `qrcode-3/09`, `low-res-v1-a.webp`, the bound's other unit case); the horizon refusal by its unit test. Full suite green on both frameworks, Release (28,463; 378 skipped on this x64 machine) and Debug (28,453, the allocation tests compiled out).

**Exit met.** Sweep against `main`, image for image, no misread: keystone 6-20 % 2,210 → 2,400 of 2,400, the gap 190 → 0; every other kind identical render for render (54,400 images); Micro QR (18,400) and rMQR (29,440) identical. Real images, against `main`:
