**Taken out, with the numbers.**

- **The frame as the first grid where nothing anchors the corner.** It lost 16 flat anti-aliased renders at 1.25-1.3 px/module (three cases, through four to six encoders each), which the parallelogram, exact for a flat symbol, had read: there a size 1-2 % off reads as perspective. It is now the grid after the parallelogram.
- **Sub-pixel sizes for the centre refinement too.** Anti-aliased 1.25-1.5 px/module +6, 1.0-1.25 +49 and −6: it changes renders that have nothing to do with keystone, so the refinement keeps its runs and the flat kinds stay identical. A lead for the low-density work, not taken here.
- **Runs weighing a line with no bound.** Two flat binarized renders at 2.6-2.8 px/module that read on `main` fail (one as `NotDetected`), and seven binarized keystoned ones the bound reads, two of which `main` reads (3.6 and 8.3 % keystone); against one real image gained (`qrcode-4/09` at 0°) and a few binarized keystone reads. The bound first tried, two thirds of a pixel, cost about 50 binarized keystone reads; a third exactly sits on the twelfths lattice and let float rounding decide (+321 −2 against +319 −0 over 4,000). Four twelfths, compared between four and five, is the runs' resolution and loses nothing against `main`.
- **The dimension estimate from each line's own sizes** (the distance over the geometric mean of the end sizes, exact under perspective): no read and no time moved on any set, since the timing count and the version information already correct the old estimate. **The mesh's first-row seeds from the frame**: no read moved in the sweep, the corpus, the 4,000-render sets or the envelope to 50 %. Both removed.
- **Darkness integrated along the line as the size**: worse than the crossings (above); it depends on the grey levels' calibration, where a crossing depends only on their midpoint.

**Left.**

- **The finders past 20 % keystone.** At 20-30 % and 3-6 px/module 13 of 400 renders fail, every one in finder detection or triple selection (5 with no three finders found, 8 with a false candidate in the chosen triple), and each reads through its true geometry; zxing-cpp reads 397. The triple's score (distance from a right isosceles triangle plus module-size spread) is what a strong keystone breaks. A score that holds under perspective, or several triples tried in turn, is its own phase: the finder's candidate list on noise is pinned by this plan's rules and the triple selection has its own lessons.
- **Real images this phase does not reach**: `qrcode-3/03` and `/22` (binarized with heavy ink spread: zxing-cpp's own corners give a grid this library's one-pixel reader does not read either), `qrcode-3/30` and `qrcode-4/12`, `/15`, `/17`, `/21`, `/29` (`NotDetected`: no three finders found). Phase 6 triages them.

**Lessons.** The diagnosis column decided again, and more narrowly than "the frame": the failing renders' finders were right, and what was wrong was one prediction extrapolated from them. The information to correct it was already measured (the module size at each finder along each line), and the plane it implies is exact; what limited it was the measurement's resolution, and the same measurement at a finer resolution moved the worst prediction from 8 modules to 2. That resolution also decides where the frame may be used: it can say where to look with a size 2 % off, and it cannot be the grid a flat symbol is sampled through. A bound derived from a measurement's lattice has to be compared off the lattice. And the pieces were kept by switching each off alone over every set, not by how principled they looked: two that were exact in theory (the dimension from each line's sizes, the frame's mesh seeds) moved nothing and went, and one that looked minor (the timing match through the frame) is worth 47 of 400 at 40-50 %.

**Benchmark delta.** BenchmarkDotNet (ShortRun, a round of each tree back to back, two rounds; the rounds differ by up to 10 % on this machine, so each is compared within itself), `main` → this phase, µs, span entry: `v40-3px` 92.5 → 85.7 and 95.7 → 93.3, `v40-3.4px` 106.1 → 95.8 and 110.2 → 108.9, `v40-4px-rot17` 270.0 → 273.2 and 307.3 → 300.4, `v40-4px-soft` 249.1 → 250.9 and 279.2 → 269.0, `v6-4px` 9.54 → 9.44 and 10.49 → 10.17, the new `v25-4px-keystone15` 196.3 → 164.6 and 193.5 → 191.7, `none-noise` 3,388 → 3,045 and 3,096 → 3,311, `none-gradient` 812 → 781 and 726 → 827; allocations unchanged. Fastest of three interleaved rounds, one thread, supersampled renders turned 23°: reads, a version 25 at 15 % keystone 411 → 173 (it anchors on the first attempt), a version 1 at 15 % keystone failing in 95 → read in 17, a version 40 at 15 % 499 → 508, a flat version 25 94.1 → 95.2 and a flat version 6 at 3 px/module 13.2 → 14.0 (the sub-pixel sizes, 0.8 µs); failures, a damaged version 1 flat 110 → 91 and keystoned 83 → 93 (the frame's grid), a damaged version 10 355 → 359, a damaged version 25 under 10 % keystone 1,318 → 1,538 (it now anchors on the real alignment pattern and runs the mesh and the fallbacks on it), 512 × 512 8-bit noise 2,915 → 2,980 and two-level noise 1,568 → 1,671 (a false triple's runs can differ past their resolution and give the frame's grid one more decode), a Micro QR image 45.6 → 45.6.

### Keystone past 20 %, investigated (2026-09-25)

**Why.** Phase 5's exit stopped at 20 %. The question after it: is the frame the best mechanism the readers have, and what limits it past 20 %? The envelope's renders (400 a cell, any turn, the same renders for every reader), read by four readers:

| Keystone, px/module | FeatherQR | zxing-cpp | ZXing.Net | CodeGlyphX, 1 s budget |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Up to 6 %, 3-6 | 400 | 400 | 296 | 106 |
| 6-20 %, 3-6 | 400 | 399 | 142 | 7 |
| 20-30 %, 3-6 | 387 | 397 | 35 | 0 |
| 30-40 %, 3-6 | 276 | 242 | 8 | 0 |
| 40-50 %, 3-6 | 171 | 29 | 0 | 0 |
| Up to 6 %, 2-3 | 400 | 388 | 155 | 25 |
| 6-20 %, 2-3 | 400 | 376 | 69 | 1 |
| 20-30 %, 2-3 | 379 | 327 | 9 | 0 |

CodeGlyphX with no budget spent over 25 CPU-seconds an image and did not finish one cell, so its column is what it reads in a second, not what it can read. Mean time per image, one thread, 100 renders, wrappers included, zxing-cpp with its harder search on, FeatherQR / zxing-cpp / ZXing.Net in ms: up to 6 % 0.30 / 2.06 / 5.3, 6-20 % 0.34 / 2.23 / 7.6, 30-40 % 0.97 / 1.90 / 9.4.

**How each gets the fourth corner.** ZXing.Net: the parallelogram with a linear correction, a window of 4, 8 then 16 modules, the ring test against the global module size, affine where no pattern is found, one triple. CodeGlyphX: the parallelogram, one fixed window, the pattern at whole pixels, the four corners extrapolated with the global vectors, then brute force over dimensions, triples and binarizations. go-qr (Go, not in the harness): affine only, no alignment search. zxing-cpp: as phase 5 recorded. The frame is the only one of them that uses the size change the finders already show, and it is not the limit anywhere measured: at 40-50 %, given the true dimension, the anchored grid of every render whose finders were right lay within 0.16 module of the drawn one.

**Where the failures are** (3-6 px/module; the first three columns are the triple the decoder chose, the last is the full sweep's candidate list against the drawn finders):

| Keystone | Failed | No three finders | A false candidate in the triple | Finders right | A drawn finder not among the candidates |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20-30 % | 13 | 5 | 8 | 0 | 11 |
| 30-40 % | 124 | 78 | 46 | 0 | 118 |
| 40-50 % | 229 | 146 | 78 | 5 | 209 |

The missing finder is the one at the wide edge, in all 338. The renderer's keystone narrows the top edge and keeps the height, so a plane in perspective draws the rows at the wide edge 1/(1 − k) times taller than they are wide (1.56 at 36 %) while the narrow edge stays square: the finder there has a column far longer than its row, and the cross-checks refuse a column whose run total is 40 % or more from the row's.

**Switched on phase 5's code, each by an environment variable, then removed** (reads of 400):

| Keystone, px/module | Phase 5 | The column's total within 5/12 to 12/5 of the row's | And the dimension from each line's sizes | zxing-cpp |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6-20 %, 3-6 | 400 | 400 | 400 | 399 |
| 20-30 %, 3-6 | 387 | 399 | 399 | 397 |
| 30-40 %, 3-6 | 276 | 387 | 387 | 242 |
| 40-50 %, 3-6 | 171 | 357 | 373 | 29 |
| 20-30 %, 2-3 | 379 | 378 | | 327 |

- **The aspect bound.** Each direction still has to pass its own 1:1:3:1:1; only the coupling between them was widened, and the walk was the reference walk with a cap of three times the row's total. Standard QR sweep 54,400 of 54,400 identical render for render with both switches on; corpus Standard QR +3 −0 (`qrcode-2`), no new misread. Its 40-50 % failures: 31 a false candidate in the triple, 12 with the finders right and a dimension 12 to 20 modules short.
- **The dimension.** Under the frame's own model the module count between two finder centres is the distance over √(s_a · s_b) exactly (the frame gives s_a = w·L/(n − 7) and s_b = L/(w·(n − 7))), and an average of the sizes is short by 2 / (w + 1/w): 6 % at a size ratio of 2, 13 % at 3. Alone, in this form, it moves 40-50 % from 171 to 180; with the aspect bound it adds 16.
- **Cost**, fastest of three interleaved runs, one thread, µs, phase 5 → the aspect bound (the dimension adds nothing past run-to-run noise): reads, a version 40 at 15 % keystone 507 → 558, a version 25 at 15 % 172 → 195, a version 1 at 15 % 17.0 → 17.2, a flat version 25 93.7 → 99.0, a flat version 6 at 3 px/module 13.9 → 14.2; failures, a damaged version 1 88 → 97 and keystoned 90 → 98, a damaged version 10 355 → 375, a damaged version 25 under 10 % keystone 1,512 → 1,588, 512 × 512 8-bit noise 2,934 → 3,493 and two-level noise 1,649 → 1,891, a Micro QR image 44.7 → 45.6. Part of it is the uncapped walk: the bounded walk reads 0.55 to 0.60 of the pixels on a refusal.
- **Not run:** the Micro QR and rMQR sweeps (the finder search is theirs too), the 4,000-render sets, the candidate counts on the two-level noise set, and zxing-cpp's other step, the version information read through the first transform before sampling. They are phase 5b's.

**Left** after both switches: 1 render at 20-30 %, 13 at 30-40 % (each with the three drawn finders among the candidates and a false one chosen) and 27 at 40-50 %.

**Lessons.** A piece removed for moving nothing was removed on sets where a stage in front of it hid its case: exact under the frame's model, the dimension from each line's sizes is worth 9 alone at 40-50 % and 16 once the stretched finder is found. "No effect" holds for the sets it was measured on, behind the stages as they were then. The frame's exactness said nothing about those stages, and the comparison was answered only stage by stage: the full sweep's candidates against the drawn finders, the triple chosen, the dimension, then the grid at the true dimension. Reading other libraries needs its own care: a reader that searches by brute force gets a stated time budget, or a cell never finishes; stopping one cell's process does not stop the loop over cells, and the next cell ran unbudgeted beside the timing runs and doubled them until it was found; zxing-cpp's native reader crashed once in a corpus run (an access violation in `ZXing_ReadBarcodes`) and the rerun was clean.
